h1: El Paso County Courts for Traffic Tickets
intro: Seven different courts handle traffic tickets in El Paso County, and each has its own prosecutor, docket and habits. Attorney Robert Navar appears in all of them for a flat fee — $59 in El Paso Municipal Court, $69 everywhere else.
summary: Who wrote the ticket decides the court. El Paso Police citations go to El Paso Municipal Court; Sheriff, constable and DPS citations go to a Justice of the Peace precinct; city police in Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton file in their own municipal courts.
Our flat fee is $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 per ticket in every JP and small-city court. Extra citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons.
The two results we work for in every court are a dismissal or a deferred disposition — both end with no conviction on your record.
In most courts the client does not appear at all. Hire online and we file the appearance the same business day.

sections.heading: Which Officer Sends You to Which Court
paragraphs: Look at the top of the citation. If it says El Paso Police Department, the case is in El Paso Municipal Court at 810 E. Overland Ave downtown — by far the busiest ticket court in the county, with multiple judges and pretrial dockets every weekday. If the officer was with the Sheriff's Office, a constable, or the Texas Department of Public Safety, the case goes to one of the Justice of the Peace precincts, and which precinct depends on where the stop happened, not where you live — a DPS ticket on I-10 near Anthony and one on Loop 375 in the Lower Valley go to different JPs.

Inside the incorporated towns, city police file in the local municipal court. Horizon City Municipal Court on Darrington Rd handles a steady volume of speeding tickets from Horizon Blvd and Eastlake. Socorro Municipal Court sees many of the Lower Valley stops along North Loop and Socorro Rd. The smaller San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton municipal courts each sit only a few days a month, which changes the timing of everything.

sections.heading: Our Flat Fee in Each El Paso County Court
paragraphs: We charge by the court because that is what drives the work. A ticket in El Paso Municipal Court is a flat $59. A ticket in any El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct is $69. Horizon City Municipal Court is $69, Socorro Municipal Court is $69, and the San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton municipal courts are $69 each. The difference reflects the drive and fewer docket dates, not a different defense.

Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons of $10 to $30 each. An existing warrant is $35 for the first and $20 for each additional, recalled as part of the same engagement — see our warrants hub. The consultation is free in every court, and the fee is the fee: no hourly billing, no surprise invoice after the docket. Hire online in about two minutes, or use the free ticket lookup if you don't know which court you're in.

sections.heading: How the Dockets Differ — and Why It Matters to Your Result
paragraphs: El Paso Municipal Court runs the way a high-volume court should: an attorney files an appearance online, gets a pretrial setting within a few weeks, and negotiates with a city prosecutor who has a standing policy on deferrals for clean records. Deferred disposition under art. 45.051 is routinely available, defensive-driving dismissals under art. 45.0511 are offered where the law allows, and a defective citation gets dismissed without much argument.

The JP precincts are a different culture. Each justice of the peace is an elected judge running a small court with their own preferences about deferral length, fees and who qualifies. DPS troopers are also more likely than city officers to show up for trial, which affects how we approach a trooper ticket. The small municipal courts sit on a limited calendar, so a case in Clint or Anthony may wait a month for its first setting; the upside is that the prosecutor and judge know us, and the negotiation is a conversation, not a form.

Whatever the court, the goals are the same. Our traffic ticket dismissal page explains the grounds we look for — missing elements, officer unavailability, proof-of-compliance dismissals for insurance and registration tickets. Our deferred adjudication and defensive driving page explains the fallback that keeps the conviction off your record, and when a judge won't offer it (25+ mph over, CDL holders, a course used in the last 12 months). The post on how to fight a traffic ticket in El Paso gives the long version.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Court Page
paragraphs: If your citation says El Paso Police, start with El Paso Municipal Court. If it says Sheriff, constable or DPS, go to El Paso County Justice of the Peace courts. For a stop by Horizon City police, see Horizon City Municipal Court; for Socorro police, Socorro Municipal Court; and for San Elizario, Clint, Anthony or Vinton police, the combined valley and upper-valley municipal courts page. For the result rather than the building, read ticket dismissal and deferred adjudication and defensive driving first.

Robert Navar was born and raised in El Paso and has appeared in every one of these courts for more than ten years. Se habla español. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case; for advice on yours, call 915-503-1600 or schedule a free consultation.

faqs.q: How do I find out which El Paso court has my ticket?
faqs.a: The agency printed on the citation tells you: El Paso Police means Municipal Court, Sheriff or DPS means a Justice of the Peace precinct, and a city police department means that city's municipal court. If you lost the ticket, the free lookup finds it.

faqs.q: Why is the fee $59 in Municipal Court but $69 in the others?
faqs.a: El Paso Municipal Court is downtown, sits every weekday and lets us file electronically. The JP precincts and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton courts are farther out and sit less often, so each case takes more time. The defense itself is the same.

faqs.q: Is deferred disposition available in every El Paso County court?
faqs.a: Generally yes, but each judge sets the terms. Municipal Court applies a fairly standard policy; JP judges and the small-city courts vary on length, fee and eligibility. We know the preferences in each and ask for the version most likely to be granted.

faqs.q: Can a ticket from a DPS trooper on I-10 be handled without me?
faqs.a: Yes. DPS tickets are filed in the JP precinct for the area of the stop, and we appear there for $69. Troopers are more likely to show for trial than city officers, so we negotiate on the pretrial docket rather than gamble on a no-show.
